title: Rational and Irrational Numbers
seo_title: Grade 8 Rational and Irrational Numbers Worksheets: Repeating Decimals, Estimating √2 and π
standard_text: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 rational and irrational numbers worksheets: classify numbers, write fractions as decimals, change repeating decimals to fractions, estimate √2 and π, place them on a number line, and order real numbers. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Rational numbers end or repeat as decimals. Irrational numbers never end and never repeat.
key_sub: √2, √3 and π are irrational. √16 = 4 and 0.333… = 1/3 are rational.
body_html:
Rational and irrational numbers

A rational number can be written as a fraction of two integers. As a decimal, it ends or repeats. An irrational number cannot: its decimal never ends and never repeats.

RationalIrrational
5, −3, 0√2, √3, √5
3/4 = 0.75π = 3.14159…
1/3 = 0.333…0.1010010001…
√16 = 4√10
Example

Write 0.4 as a fraction.

Let x = 0.444….

10x = 4.444….

Subtract: 9x = 4, so x = 4/9.

Answer: 4/9

Example

Estimate √20.

4² = 16 and 5² = 25, so √20 is between 4 and 5.

4.5² = 20.25, so √20 is a bit less than 4.5.

Answer: about 4.47

Common mistakes

  • Calling every root irrational: √25 = 5 is rational.
  • Calling every long decimal irrational: 0.333… repeats, so it is rational.
  • Writing 0.333… as 3/10. It is 1/3.
  • Thinking π = 3.14 exactly. 3.14 is only an estimate.

faq.q: What is the difference between rational and irrational numbers?
faq.a: A rational number can be written as a fraction of integers, and its decimal ends or repeats. An irrational number cannot; its decimal never ends and never repeats, like √2 or π.
Yes. Every repeating decimal can be written as a fraction. For example, 0.444… = 4/9.
No. The square root of a perfect square is rational: √49 = 7. √2 and √10 are irrational.

faq.q: How do you change a repeating decimal to a fraction?
faq.a: Let x be the decimal. Multiply by 10 (or 100 for two repeating digits) and subtract to remove the repeating part. 0.444…: 10x − x = 4, so x = 4/9.
